candidates.original_title: Entry regulation and entrepreneurship: a natural experiment in German craftsmanship
candidates.description: The effect of deregulation of the German Trade and Crafts Code of 2004 on market entry, self-employment, and exit probabilities in crafts trades
candidates.citation_sentence: Rostam-Afschar (2014, RA hereafter) examines the effects of the deregulation of occupational licensing in the German crafts sector.
candidates.notes: RA found no change in exit probabilities; replication found significant increase of 2.0-2.5pp in B1-trades

candidates.original_title: Entry regulation and entrepreneurship: a natural experiment in German craftsmanship
candidates.description: The 2004 deregulation of German crafts trades does not change exit probabilities in fully deregulated or partially deregulated trades.
candidates.citation_sentence: Using microcensus data, RA (2014) finds a uniformly positive effect of the reform on market entry and self-employment in the fully deregulated and partly deregulated groups. The author also finds no change in exit probabilities. Against this background, our study replicates RA's paper.
candidates.notes: The replication reports a positive and statistically significant increase in exit probabilities for fully deregulated B1-trades, contrary to the original null finding.

candidates.original_title: Entry regulation and entrepreneurship: a natural experiment in German craftsmanship
candidates.description: The 2004 deregulation of German crafts trades increases the probability of being self-employed in both fully deregulated B1-trades and partially deregulated A-trades.
candidates.citation_sentence: Using microcensus data, RA (2014) finds a uniformly positive effect of the reform on market entry and self-employment in the fully deregulated and partly deregulated groups. The author also finds no change in exit probabilities. Against this background, our study replicates RA's paper.
candidates.notes: The replication reports positive and significant effects on self-employment for both B1- and A-trades, although the B1 effect is more pronounced. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]
